correctness.rationale: Every closed-neighborhood trace equals the union of endpoint stars in the selected edge graph. Shattered empty trace forces two outside ground vertices; shattered singletons force each selected edge to meet a leaf, hence the selected graph is a star forest. Full-trace and intermediate-trace witnesses rule out more than two components, stars of degree >=4, and a degree-three star with a second component. The remaining six types realize all subsets with at most two vertex stars. Exact labelled placement counts yield all polynomial coefficients and thresholds. A standalone Python checker tests 763914 selected sets in bounded dimensions, confirming but not replacing the all-n proof.

Relevant inspected prior primary results establish the open-neighborhood VC dimension on Johnson graphs or generic closed-neighborhood VC tools, not these closed-neighborhood statements. value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact structural and coefficientwise shattering classification for the natural rank-two Johnson line graph family at arbitrary size. It makes a precise distinction between open and closed neighborhoods by a sharp different first dimension attaining VC dimension four, a mathematically natural boundary relevant to finite-model-theoretic graph set systems; it is neither mere normalization nor a single arbitrary numerical slice.
